system.name: Gigaflow
system.one_liner: a SmartNIC caching system that caches reusable sub-traversals of a vSwitch pipeline instead of whole flows

components.name: Input Flow (F)
components.role: the incoming packet's flow signature (header fields) that misses the LTM cache and is sent to the vSwitch

components.name: vSwitch
components.role: software virtual switch whose userspace pipeline builds the traversal for a flow that misses the SmartNIC cache

components.name: Userspace Forwarding Pipeline
components.role: processes the flow signature through the vSwitch pipeline tables, producing the unrolled traversal (tables Ti, modified flow Fi, wildcard Wi)

components.name: Sub-Traversal Partition Generation
components.role: divides the traversal into up to K disjoint sub-traversals, selecting the partitioning that maximizes disjointness

components.name: LTM Rule Creation & Installation
components.role: converts sub-traversals into LTM rules (match predicate Mk, wildcard ωk, priority ρk, table tag τk, action αk) and installs them into the cache

components.name: SmartNIC
components.role: hardware device hosting the Gigaflow LTM cache and processing matched packets at line rate

components.name: GF1...GFK
components.role: K feed-forward P4-programmable RMT lookup tables that together implement Longest Traversal Match (LTM) caching of installed sub-traversal rules

components.name: Longest Traversal Match (LTM)
components.role: the matching mechanism, implemented across GF1...GFK, that uses rule priority and table-tag metadata to select the correct cached sub-traversal path

content.key_idea: Gigaflow partitions each flow's vSwitch pipeline traversal into disjoint, shareable sub-traversals cached as prioritized, tagged LTM rules across K SmartNIC tables, and a worked example shows how missing priority or table-tag metadata causes incorrect matches or paths.
content.reading_order: Left to right: input flow into the vSwitch pipeline, sub-traversal partitioning and rule installation, down into the SmartNIC's GF1...GFK caches; then the notation key and worked example on the right.

summary: This figure presents Gigaflow's high-level architecture and a worked example of its caching mechanism. On the left, an incoming flow's signature is processed through the vSwitch's userspace forwarding pipeline to produce a traversal of accessed tables; Sub-Traversal Partition Generation splits this into up to K disjoint sub-traversals, and LTM Rule Creation & Installation converts them into rules (with a match predicate, wildcard, priority, table tag, and action) installed into K SmartNIC lookup tables, GF1 through GFK, that implement Longest Traversal Match (LTM) caching. A middle panel defines the traversal and rule notation, and a right panel walks through two example traversals sharing a prefix, showing with colored paths and callout text how omitting rule priority or table-tag metadata causes incorrect matches or paths. The figure mixes Office-blue/orange highlighted step boxes, math notation, and an annotated worked example in one dense, double-column-width layout.
summary_zh: 该图展示 Gigaflow 架构：流量经 vSwitch 用户态转发流水线生成遍历路径，经子遍历划分与 LTM 规则生成安装到 SmartNIC 的 GF1...GFK 缓存表中；右侧示例说明缺少优先级或表标签会导致匹配或路径错误。
